question.problem:
Suppose that the function $f(x,y)$ and all of its first and second-order partial derivatives are continuous on an open set $U.$ Find the values of $a$ and $b$, if 

$$
{f}_{x}(x,y)=2y\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)+a{y}^{2},\,{f}_{y}(x,y)=bx\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)+6xy.
$$
question.worked_solution:
First, we find the mixed partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xy}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({f}_{x}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2y\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)+a{y}^{2}) \\  & =2\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)-2yx\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy)+2ay \\ {f}_{yx}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({f}_{y}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(bx\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)+6xy) \\  & =b\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)-bxy\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy)+6y\end{aligned}
$$

Since the function and its first and second-order partial derivatives are continuous on an open set $U,$ the mixed partial derivatives must be equal. Hence, we have the identity

$$
\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)-2yx\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy)+2ay & =b\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)-bxy\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy)+6y.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the coefficients of $y$ and $\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy),$ respectively, we see that $a=3$ and $b=2.$
